newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian minister suspended in video scandal-PM.
newsitem.headline: Russian minister suspended in video scandal-PM.

text.p: Russia's justice minister, caught up in a scandal over a video film showing sauna scenes, will be removed from office temporarily, Interfax news agency quoted Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin as saying on Sunday.

"Chernomyrdin reports that Justice Minister (Valentin) Kovalyov will be temporarily suspended from carrying out his official duties," Interfax said. Kovalyov asked President Boris Yeltsin on Saturday to suspend him while he cleared his name.

Kovalyov's request was an unusual step in Russian politics and came after the monthly newspaper Sovershenno Sekretno (Top Secret) published grainy snaps taken from the video which it alleged showed him in a night-club sauna with women.

Chernomyrdin, speaking to reporters after laying a wreath at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier in Moscow, described the developments as "sad". The prime minister recalled Kovalyov from a foreign trip on Friday when the story broke.
"Kovalyov denies everything," Chernomyrdin said. "He is a lawyer he knows how to defend himself. Let him prove it is not true."
Kovalyov said in a statement on Saturday he had nothing to be ashamed of and would defend his good name.
